original_question: For the variety IMMr,V ⊆ P(S^dV) of homogeneous polynomials admitting an algebraic branching program of width at most r, determine defining equations for small r and small dim(V).
target_in_paper: Problem 17 in Section 3.2 (Variety of ABPs of small width): Determine equations for IMM_{r,V} ⊆ P(S^dV) for small values of r and dim V.
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's intended problem very closely: it names the correct variety IMM_{r,V}, places it in the correct ambient projective space P(S^dV), keeps the homogeneous-polynomial/algebraic-branching-program viewpoint, and asks for defining equations in exactly the small-r, small-dim(V) regime singled out in Problem 17.
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers C.
V is a finite-dimensional complex vector space, and P(S^dV) means the projective space of lines in S^dV.
S^dV is identified with the space of degree-d homogeneous polynomials on V^*, so the ambient polynomial space should be stated explicitly.
The relevant complexity measure is the iterated matrix multiplication complexity imm_C(f), not only the informal phrase 'admits an algebraic branching program of width at most r.'

imm_C(f) is defined as the least integer r such that f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in V ⊗ Mat_{1×r}(C), M_j in V ⊗ Mat_{r×r}(C) for 2 ≤ j ≤ d-1, and M_d in V ⊗ Mat_{r×1}(C); equivalently, the matrix entries are linear forms.
The variety is projective, so its points are classes [f] with imm_C(f) ≤ r.
The problem asks for defining equations of the Zariski-closed variety IMM_{r,V}, not for its dimension and not for a border version.
The degree d is part of the data and the problem stays in the homogeneous setting; the paper does not additionally restrict d to be small.
The phrase 'small values of r and dim V' is intentionally qualitative in the paper; there is no further asymptotic quantifier such as 'for all sufficiently large m'.
No nilpotency condition appears in the paper's formulation; adding one would change the problem.
refined_question: Over C, let V be a finite-dimensional vector space and let d ≥ 1. Identify S^dV with the space of degree-d homogeneous polynomials on V^*. For a homogeneous polynomial f in S^dV, define imm_C(f) to be the least integer r such that f can be written as f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in V ⊗ Mat_{1×r}(C), M_j in V ⊗ Mat_{r×r}(C) for 2 ≤ j ≤ d-1, and M_d in V ⊗ Mat_{r×1}(C). Equivalently, imm_C(f) is the minimum width of an algebraic branching program for f. Define IMM_{r,V} := { [f] in P(S^dV) : imm_C(f) ≤ r }. Determine defining equations for the projective variety IMM_{r,V} for small values of r and dim V.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for small values of r and dim V, determine defining equations for the projective variety of degree-d homogeneous polynomials on V^* that admit an algebraic branching program of width at most r.
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 3.2 rather than any other part of the paper. In Section 3.1, the paper defines the iterated matrix multiplication complexity imm_C(f) for homogeneous f in S^d C^N via a product of matrices whose entries are linear forms. In Section 3.2, it then defines IMM_{r,V} = { [f] in P(S^dV) : imm_C(f) ≤ r }, notes that this set is Zariski closed, and poses Problem 17 exactly as determining equations for IMM_{r,V} for small values of r and dim V. To make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the rewrite restores the ambient field C, the projective and homogeneous setting, and the precise matrix-factorization definition of ABP width. The nearby context also makes clear that the paper is not asking for a border analogue, a nilpotency variant, or an asymptotic statement beyond the qualitative phrase 'small values of r and dim V.'
